ranked.lever: Triple Hook (Context: the wish. Pull: 'But real benefit?' Whiplash: 'Stiff people.')
ranked.spoken: Everybody want naturally flexible body. But real benefit? Stiff people.
ranked.visual: First frame: a flexible student folds flat in Paschimottanasana (seated forward fold), chest on the legs, easy and still. On 'Stiff people', hard cut to a stiff student in the same asana, hands far from the feet, calm breath. Gold word: STIFF. Small pause before 'Stiff people', said flat. Both students filmed in the shala with their OK.
ranked.reason: Scores: scroll stop 8, true to his words 10, mirror 9, his voice 9. Every word comes from his own two lines: 'Everyone want to have naturally flexible body' and 'That's the real benefit!' With sound off, the text flips what everyone expects in five words, and the hard cut from the flat fold to the stiff student shows that flip, so the eye gets it before the ear does. The stiff beginner expects the teacher to praise the bendy body. Instead the prize goes to them ('that's me, and I'm welcome here'). The flexible student stays to find out what they are missing. It opens a loop that the draft's 'That's the real benefit' beat at second 30 closes, so the script body still works. One fix: at his pace the spoken line runs about 4 to 5 seconds. Let 'Stiff people' land exactly on the cut at second 3, or drop 'naturally' when he speaks (keep it in the caption).

ranked.spoken: "I'm not flexible." Okay. You learn every part of your body.
ranked.visual: Sound: no music for the first second, only loud ujjayi breath. First frame: a side-view extreme close-up of a student's fingertips in Paschimottanasana, stopping a hand's width before the toes. No face, so any student can say yes to filming. Hard cut to Boonchu's face on 'Okay.' He says the first line as the viewer's own thought, then 'Okay' flat and kind, not as a joke.
ranked.reason: Scores: scroll stop 9, true to his words 7, mirror 10, his voice 8. This is the strongest pure mirror. In second 1 the stiff beginner reads their own thought over fingertips that do not reach, which is their own body. Breath with no music breaks the feed. The kind 'Okay' gives permission, which is very welcoming. It loses points on truth to his words: it leaves out the flexible half and his 'real benefit' line, so the comparison he asked about only starts after second 3. With sound off, 'Okay.' on its own can also read as cold. Put 'You learn every part.' on screen at 1.5 s so it reads as acceptance. Use this one if he wants a pure 'I'm not flexible' fear buster.

ranked.spoken: Everybody want flexible body. But stiff people get the real benefit.
ranked.visual: Boonchu talks to camera in the shala. First frame: behind him, a flexible student folds flat in Paschimottanasana. On 'But stiff people', whip-pan to a stiff student in the same asana, hands on the shins, calm and breathing.
ranked.reason: Scores: scroll stop 7, true to his words 10, mirror 8, his voice 8. Same true flip as the winner, using his exact phrase 'the real benefit'. But the first frame is a talking head with the student small in the background, so it stops fewer thumbs. He also says the answer in one flat sentence with no pause, so there is less pull. On screen, 'Stiff body, real benefit' reads like a label, not a surprise. It is a good backup if he wants to say the hook in one breath.

ranked.spoken: Which one you want? Naturally flexible... or stiff, learn to bend?
ranked.visual: One wide shot from the side, no edit needed. First frame: two students on mats next to each other in Paschimottanasana. The left one folds flat, the right one holds the shins. Both faces are calm, both are breathing, so nobody looks like the loser. The text sits between them.
ranked.reason: Scores: scroll stop 6, true to his words 10, mirror 8, his voice 10. It is his own question word for word, and every viewer finds their own body on one of the two mats. But a question as the first line is easy to scroll past. Without sound, 'or learn it?' is unclear, and one wide shot with no change in 3 seconds gives the eye nothing new. It also spends his ending early: the draft closes on this exact question at second 33, so he would ask it twice.

ranked.spoken: You say, 'I'm not flexible.' Or, 'I bend, no control.'
ranked.visual: 0 to 1.5 s: low shot of a student's fingers hanging far above the floor in Uttanasana (standing forward fold). 1.5 to 3 s: hard cut to a flexible student holding one leg high in Utthita Hasta Padangusthasana, easy, while the standing leg wobbles. Gold word: FLEXIBLE. Real students, filmed with their OK.
ranked.reason: Scores: scroll stop 7, true to his words 6, mirror 9, his voice 6. It names both viewers in the first 3 seconds, which is good for the mirror. But 'I bend, no control' puts a flat claim in the flexible student's mouth, and his word was 'might not'. Two cuts and two different asanas in 3 seconds is busy. Spoken out loud, a quote inside a quote is hard to follow by ear. On screen, 'no control' as a label can feel like a put-down to flexible students.

hooks.pick_reason: The Triple Hook ('Everybody want naturally flexible body. But real benefit? Stiff people.') wins because it is the only hook that scores high on all four tests. Every word is Boonchu's own, so there is nothing to fact-check and no medical claim. On screen, 'The real benefit? Stiff people.' plus the cut from the flat fold to the stiff student flips what everyone expects, and it works with the sound off. The stiff beginner gets the prize in the first 3 seconds, so they think 'that's me' and feel invited. The flexible viewer stays to find out what they are missing. It also sets up his own payoff at second 30 ('That's the real benefit'), so the draft only needs the timing fix in the reason. The Pattern Interrupt is a close second and is the better choice for a pure 'I'm not flexible' fear-buster Reel. Why the rest lost: the Two-Voice Deadpan is a joke bit (his lines must not be a joke), and 'hold it' is not his idea. 'Not about who bends deeper' is not his claim, and it clashes with his ending 'I also wanna be naturally flexible'. The Stakes and Split-Screen hooks speak to the flexible student, not the stiff beginner, and the split screen films a student shaking. The Authority hook's 'both pay a price' and 'I teach many years' are not his words. One note for the script body (separate from the hooks): the draft's second 9 to 12 line says 'they can't control the flexibility', but he said 'might not be able to control'. Change it to 'they might not control it' so it stays a teacher's observation.

blocks.problem: A stiff beginner with sound off sees only a flexible student folding flat and the word FLEXIBLE with a gift emoji. That is not them, so there is no 'oh, that's me', and the gift emoji means nothing without sound. The stiff body (the viewer's mirror) does not show up until 12 s.
blocks.better_visual: Two mats side by side in the shala, both in Paschimottanasana: a flexible student folds flat, easy. Next to them a stiff beginner, hands at the shins, far from the feet. Stiff mat in front, so the viewer sees themselves first.

blocks.problem: With sound off, THE PROBLEM? is too vague to open a real loop. 'Nobody talk about it' is not in Boonchu's words. It is an invented claim, and a cliche.
blocks.better_spoken: But natural flexible people... they have problem.
blocks.better_visual: Punch in 1.3x on your face (house cut zoom) with a sound hit. The text card pops in over the frozen flat fold from block 1.

blocks.problem: The surprise holds: the easy bender struggles where strength is needed. But this idea is split across two blocks (6-12). STRENGTH with a muscle emoji does not explain anything with sound off. Showing a real student 'failing' needs their OK and kind framing. Merge with 9-12 into one block of about 4 s (6-10).
blocks.better_spoken: When they need the strength... they might not control their flexibility.
blocks.better_visual: Same flexible student (with their OK) goes from the flat fold straight into the lift-up (Utpluthih) or a jump back: hands press, body shakes, feet stay down. Real speed, no slow-mo, no laugh sound. Film it as trying, not failing.

blocks.problem: Same picture again in slow-mo, so there is no new visual. It drops Boonchu's 'might' and turns his teacher observation into an absolute ('they can't control'). CONTROL with a red X reads like a verdict on a real student. It also stalls the video.

This is the strongest mirror moment for a stiff beginner, but it comes too late and only fills half a block. The brick emoji can feel like teasing the viewer. Merge with 15-18 so stiff people get one fast block (about 10-13 s) that calls back to the stiff mat from block 1.
blocks.better_spoken: Stiff people? They must learn to bend... every section.
blocks.better_visual: Hard cut back to the stiff beginner from block 1, then quick 0.5 s cuts on different students: hips, hamstrings, shoulders, back, each one working at their edge.

blocks.problem: The quick cuts work well (a new picture every half second). The spoken line drifts from his words: he said 'every sections'. On its own it repeats the previous block, so it is merged into 12-15 above.
blocks.better_spoken: MERGED into 12-15 above (keep the quick cuts there).

blocks.problem: This mirrors the stiff beginner well ('it IS hard for me'). But THE HARD WAY in big text with a serious face could scare a beginner, and it closes flat with no loop into the next block. 'Piece by piece' is not his wording. Use his line, show a smiling teacher helping, and end the text on 'BUT' to pull into the next block.
blocks.better_visual: Teacher kneels beside the stiff beginner and gives a gentle adjustment in the forward fold. Small change, both smiling. The beginner is clearly supported, not alone.

blocks.problem: A close-up of a face or breath with EVERY BIT means nothing with sound off, and it is the second face shot in a row. Paraphrased: his word is 'absorb', not 'feel'. Merge with 24-27 into one block (about 16-19 s).
blocks.better_spoken: But they absorb every bit. Every move... every improvement.
blocks.better_visual: Right after the adjustment, close-up on the stiff beginner's hands sliding a little closer to the feet, in real time, same session. Only use a 'before and after' if it is real old footage of the same student. Never stage it as months of progress.

blocks.problem: The progress picture is good, but THEY KNOW IT is vague with sound off. 'Every small progress' repeats the block before. It is merged into 21-24 above.

This is the turn, and it works for a stiff beginner (my stiffness becomes a gift). EVERY STIFF PERSON is half a sentence with sound off. 'One day' and 'in the room' are small additions; keep to his line.
blocks.better_spoken: So they know... and understand every stiff people.
blocks.better_visual: Wide shot of the full Mysore room, all body types, then a slow push in to a beginner reaching for the toes (one more 'that's me' for the viewer).

blocks.problem: Passes. It is the payoff, kept for the end (REVEAL AT THE END). Add the house cut zoom and a 1 s silent beat after the line before the question, so it lands.
blocks.better_visual: Back to your face, still, 1.3x punch on 'real benefit' with a chime, then hold 1 s in silence.

blocks.problem: Passes, and the split screen is the right picture. But Boonchu's own 'let me know your thoughts' is missing from the spoken line (it only lives in the caption). The line is about 13 words, so give it 4 s.
blocks.better_spoken: So which one you want? Natural flexible... or tight, then learn to bend? Let me know.
blocks.better_visual: Split screen: the flexible student's flat fold on the left, the stiff beginner's fold on the right (the same two from block 1, which closes the loop).

blocks.problem: The joke works with sound, but with sound off 'ME?' and a hand emoji do not carry it. A silent viewer never learns what he picks.
blocks.better_spoken: For me... I also wanna be naturally flexible.
blocks.better_visual: Your face, small smile, cut zoom on 'naturally flexible' with a pop sound.

blocks.problem: Keep the close (his joke is good), but '(no text)' kills the punchline for sound-off viewers. They need the words to get the joke.
blocks.better_spoken: I will deal with the strength later.
blocks.better_visual: Your face, flat deadpan, hold 1 s after the last word. Stop. No music sting.

audit.overall: I checked the draft with the Missy Elliott method: every 3-second block, sound off, from a stiff beginner's seat. Two main problems: (1) For the first 12 s it only talks about flexible people, so a stiff beginner gets no 'oh, that's me' until block 5. Fix: put the stiff beginner on the mat next to the flexible student in block 1, with the text WISH YOU WERE FLEXIBLE?. Then call back to the same two people in the stiff blocks and the split-screen question. (2) Three lines go beyond Boonchu's words: 'Nobody talk about it' is invented, 'they can't control' drops his 'might', and the close has no on-screen text, so sound-off viewers miss the joke. LENGTH: the draft is 14 blocks, about 42 s. Merge 6-9 with 9-12 (and cut the slow-mo repeat), 12-15 with 15-18, and 21-24 with 24-27. That gives 11 blocks, about 34 s: 0-3 hook, 3-6 problem, 6-10 strength/control, 10-13 stiff every part, 13-16 hard way but, 16-19 absorb every bit, 19-22 understand stiff people, 22-25 real benefit plus 1 s silence, 25-29 question plus 'let me know', 29-31 me flexible, 31-34 strength later plus hold. Every block ends on an open question or a 'but' that pulls into the next one. Keep the close: his joke works once it has text. Welcome rule: show the teacher smiling and helping in the 'hard way' block, film the flexible student trying (with their OK, no slow-mo, no laugh), and drop the brick emoji. Everything can be filmed in the shala. Outside the table: the 'Toolkit pick' line has no 'Why:' line yet, which the standing order asks for. Caption line 2 ('a flexible body has a problem: control') also drops 'might'. Suggest: 'A flexible body might find control hard when it needs strength.' findings.line: 11 and 13 (spoken 3-6 s and 9-12 s); caption line 27
findings.problem: Two claims go beyond Boonchu's words. 'Nobody talk about it' is new; he never said it, and it was only added to fit the 'Dark' pull. 'They can't control the flexibility' and the caption's 'a flexible body has a problem' both drop his 'might', so his teacher observation becomes a rule about every flexible person. Flexible students will feel attacked.
findings.fix: 3-6 s spoken: 'But natural flexible... it come with a problem.' (on screen: THE PROBLEM? 🤔). 9-12 s spoken: '...they might not control the flexibility.' (on screen: CONTROL? 🤔, no ❌). Caption line 27: 'But flexible people might not be able to control it when they need strength.'

findings.problem: A real flexible student is shown failing a lift-up. The wobble is replayed in slow motion and labelled CONTROL ❌. That makes a student the joke (the Gervais rule says never a student). It also stages proof that Boonchu never claimed. Flexible students in the shala will feel singled out.
findings.fix: 6-9 s: show a house-style graphic card instead of student footage (navy card, gold title 'FLEXIBLE 🎁 + STRENGTH ?'). 9-12 s: punch in on Boonchu's face. Use the flexible student only at 0-3 s (the easy fold) and in the 33-36 s split screen, both at their best.

findings.line: 14, 18, 19 (on-screen text and pictures, 12-15 s, 18-21 s, 27-30 s)
findings.problem: Three labels make stiff beginners feel judged. 'STIFF 🧱' puts a brick on a real student whose hands are far from her feet. 'THE HARD WAY' in big letters feeds the Lane B fear 'too hard'. 'EVERY STIFF PERSON' over a wide shot of the whole Mysore room calls every student in the room stiff.
findings.fix: 12-15 s on screen: 'STIFF? 🙋' (a raised hand reads as 'that's me'). 18-21 s on screen: 'PIECE BY PIECE 🧩' (he still says 'The hard way'). 27-30 s on screen: 'THEY UNDERSTAND 🤝' over the same stiff student, smiling and a bit deeper, not over the full room.

findings.problem: This breaks the MIRROR RULE and leaves a 3-second gap with nothing new. All the stiff beats say 'they', so the viewer watches other people instead of thinking 'oh, that's me'. The fear this Reel is meant to bust ('I'm not flexible') is never said. Four 'every...' blocks in a row (EVERY PART, EVERY BIT, THEY KNOW IT, EVERY STIFF PERSON) give no new reason to keep watching.
findings.fix: Spoken, in his English: 12-15 s 'And stiff people? You think, I'm not flexible.' / 15-18 s 'You must learn to bend. Every part of your body.' / 18-21 s 'The hard way. Piece by piece.' / 21-24 s 'But you feel every bit. Every move, every small progress.' / 24-27 s 'Then you know and understand every stiff or tight people.' / 27-30 s 'That's the real benefit.' This removes one repeated block, so the Reel ends about 3 s sooner.

Choices:
- No gendered first person. "Me too" became เราก็เหมือนกัน. "Tell me below" became บอกกันหน่อยในคอมเมนต์. "I'll send you the link" became เราจะส่งลิงก์ให้. There is no ผม or ฉัน anywhere.
- I used the rule wording for "from zero": เราสอนตั้งแต่เริ่มต้น ไม่เป็นอะไรเลย. The caption never says Mysore or asana, so the มายซอร์ and อาสนะ rules do not come up.
- Stiff/flexible: ร่างกายที่ยืดหยุ่น and ร่างกายที่ตึง follow the English "flexible body / stiff body". For "every stiff person" I used คนตัวตึง, the everyday word. I kept "a problem: control" as a plain teacher observation (มีปัญหา คือการควบคุม) and made no medical claim.
- Promo: ซื้อ 1 แถม 1 สำหรับแพ็กเกจ 1, 2 หรือ 3 เดือน. "Keep both for yourself" became ใช้เองทั้งคู่ก็ได้. The deadline is 11 พ.ย., which matches the 2 Oct final rule (never 12 Nov). The promo comes first and Sharathji comes last, as the 3 Oct order says.
- For the honour line I used (เพื่อน้อมรำลึกถึงการจากไปของชารัทจี). น้อมรำลึก is a respectful way to say remembering. A word-for-word "เป็นเกียรติแด่การจากไป" sounds wrong in Thai. ชารัทจี is the spelling from the earlier Thai caption.
- "Come learn Ashtanga" became มาเรียนอัษฎางคะกับเรา, using อัษฎางคะ from the 1 Oct Thai caption.
- I kept "Comment aybkk" as คอมเมนต์ aybkk. Aybkk.com and the hashtags are unchanged. The 1 Oct Thai caption swapped in #อัษฎางคะ, but this task says to keep the hashtags.
- Spelling: โปรโมชั่น (the spelling most people use, not the official โปรโมชัน), แพ็กเกจ, ลิงก์. There are no long dashes. Long lines are split so each line is short.

Flags on the English draft (outside this task):
1. The spoken line at 9-12, "...they can't control the flexibility.", turns Boonchu's "might not be able to control" into a firm claim. A softer line in his voice: "...they might not control it."
2. The line at 3-6, "Nobody talk about it.", is a claim he did not make.
3. The 1 Oct Thai caption in bots/posts/2026-10-01-plato-mysore-reel.md breaks the newer rules (ไมซอร์, ตั้งแต่ศูนย์, ผม). Do not copy wording from it.

I checked the caption against the English caption in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-aybkk-workshop/5fef75e8-f96a-51ec-a2b6-837dec39c8e1/scratchpad/flex_script.md. The meaning matched already, so these changes are about natural Thai, clearer wording and tone.

1. Lines 1, 3, 5: changed "ร่างกายที่ยืดหยุ่น / ร่างกายที่ตึง" to "คนตัวอ่อน / คนตัวตึง". This is how Thai yoga people actually talk. It also matches the "ตัวตึง" already used in line 6. The old line 5 to 6 had "a body understands every stiff person", which sounds odd in Thai; with "คนตัวตึง" as the subject it reads correctly.
2. Line 2: "เราก็เหมือนกัน" became "เราเองก็อยากเหมือนกัน". It reads better as a reply to "อยาก" in line 1, and it still uses เรา (no ผม/ฉัน).
3. Lines 3 to 4: "ก็มีปัญหา / คือการควบคุม" became "ก็มีปัญหานะ / คือเรื่องการควบคุมร่างกาย". The old version was too stiff and didn't say what is being controlled. It stays a teacher's observation, with no medical claim.
4. Line 5: "ต้องเรียนรู้ทุกส่วน" became "ต้องเรียนรู้ร่างกายทุกส่วน", so the object is clear. I kept "แบบยากๆ" for "the hard way" because it's natural and casual.
5. Line 7: "เป็นแบบไหน?" became "ตัวอ่อนหรือตัวตึง?". The choice is now clear when the caption is read without the video, and each reader can see themselves in one side.
6. Line 8: the required phrase "เราสอนตั้งแต่เริ่มต้น ไม่เป็นอะไรเลย" is unchanged, word for word.
7. Line 11: "ใช้เองทั้งคู่" became "เก็บไว้ใช้เองทั้งสองแพ็กเกจ". In Thai, "ทั้งคู่" usually means two people, so the old line could be read as "both of you use it". The new wording says "both packages", which is what "keep both for yourself" means.
8. Line 12, respect and no hard sell:
   - "ซื้อภายใน" became "สมัครได้ถึง". It's softer and less pushy right next to a memorial, and the meaning (the offer ends 11 Nov) is the same.

Dropping "เพื่อ" also avoids "เพื่อน้อม" being misread as "เพื่อน" (friend). Sharath Jois passed away on 11 Nov 2024, so 11 Nov 2026 is the anniversary.
